summary: Botetourt County allows data centers at Greenfield business park. Greenfield is the only area in the county’s Research and Advanced Manufacturing zoning district. The zoning decision does not issue grading, building or air permits. Troutville has its own zoning rules.
locator: November 26, 2024: Zoning Ordinance Amendment Approved (county timeline)
evidence: voted to amend the County's zoning ordinance to permit data centers in the Research and Advanced Manufacturing (RAM) zoning district.

summary: The Board reports that it approved the B-1 amendment changing data centers from by right to conditional use. This was case 26-037; the November notice on definitions and energy facilities concerns a different case. The recap does not enumerate the recommended conditions or give a separate effective date.
locator: October 21, 2026 Board meeting recap, p. 1; case 26-037, § 9-1-40
evidence: Conditional Use Permit in the Business (B-1) Zoning District

summary: The county reports its updated zoning ordinance ended by-right development of new data center projects and requires a conditional-use permit. The same page describes setbacks and noise limits negotiated on named rezonings; those conditions are not encoded as countywide requirements.
locator: Data Center Development in Chesterfield; county account of zoning update; effective January 1, 2026 (ZO-2025-001)

summary: Henrico reclassified principal data centers as industrial services. In its industrial M districts, table symbol P denotes a provisional use permit, not by-right permission. Read this edition’s table legend and the parcel’s zoning and prior approvals.
locator: Ord. 1343, § 24-4205, principal use table and legend; industrial services
evidence: Provisional Use Permit for Data Centers

summary: A data center needs public water and sewer. If it uses water cooling, it must use a closed-loop or recycled water system unless the provisional use permit authorizes another system.

Under this local land-use standard, generators may run for emergency power outages or for testing and maintenance. The latter activities are limited to Monday through Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; this rule does not supply a state air permit.
locator: Ord. 1343, § 24-4328(B)(2), p. 3 (local operating schedule, separate from DEQ)

summary: An accessory data center must serve an office or industrial use on the same or adjacent premises and meet the operating and enclosure/screening standards. A principal data center does not qualify merely by being next to an office.
locator: Ord. 1343, § 24-4438(A)–(B), p. 5; consult table 4402 for permitted districts

summary: Troutville prohibits the dedicated data-center facilities defined in § 240-95 in all town zoning districts. Apply the text only within incorporated town boundaries; do not transfer it to Botetourt County. The posted text does not specify an effective date.
evidence: Data Centers are prohibited within all zoning districts
Special Permit process that addresses potential health and safety impacts
summary: Phoenix adopted a special zoning permit process for data centers. City review considers power reliability, fire risk, emergency access and noise. The zoning permit does not by itself approve construction.

evidence: Temporary Moratorium on the Issuance of Improvement location permits
summary: On August 31, 2026, Wabash County paused applications and permits for data center projects in its unincorporated zoning districts. The pause ends when new rules take effect or after 18 months, whichever comes first. LaFontaine, Lagro and Roann would each have to adopt it separately.
